CLI.domain.text: What is the climate domain? (e.g., climate denial, wildfires)

CLI.focus.text: Is a climate subject the main focus of the paper, or is it a case study?

CON.STEM_hum.text: Overall, to which research area do the contributions and methods of the study belong to?

CON.concl.text: What are the conclusions of the study? Cite them verbatim.

CON.concl_clear.text: Is there a clear conclusion in terms of climate, misinformation, or polarization besides just an improvement on machine learning metrics?

CON.concl_clear_cite.text: Which passage states it? Cite and/or explain.

CON.limits.text: What are the limitations of the study? Cite them

CON.motiv_match.condition: MOT.motiv_cite!='not reported' AND CON.concl not in ('not reported', 'unclear')
labels: 3 = addressed with explicit reflection on what was and wasn't achieved
CON.motiv_match.text: Do the motivations and conclusions match?

DA.annot.text: Did they perform annotations or produce labelled data?

DA.annot_model.condition: DA.annot_who in ('LLM or generative model', 'non-generative classifier')
labels: prelabel (the model pre-labels with human review)
voter (treated as one annotator among humans, aggregated by vote or averaging)
DA.annot_model.text: How were LLMs or other models used for annotations?

labels: study participants (survey respondents labeling their own beliefs or content)
derived from data (labels come from a signal already in the data)

DA.data_type.text: What kind of data do they use?

DA.dataset_name.text: What is the name of the dataset?

DA.end.text: What is the time span ending?

DA.geo.text: Which geographic location does the data refer to?

DA.is_data.text: Does the study uses at least one dataset in their analysis?

labels: existing dataset extended with new data or annotations
subset or sample of an existing dataset

DA.platform.text: From which platform was the data retrieved?

DA.size.text: What is the size of the dataset?

DA.size_unit.text: In which unit is the size expressed?

DA.start.text: What is the time span starting?

DA.task.text: What is the ML task the dataset is intended for?

MIS.agent_identification.text: How are the agents identified? (How do they know they created or produced the misinformation?)

MIS.agents.text: Which agents of misinformation are mentioned, if any? An agent is the individual or group that creates and/or distributes the message (e.g., a political organisation, the government, an influencer, a media organisation, a public figure)

MIS.def.text: What definition of misinformation does the study state? Cite it.

MIS.def_src.text: What is the source of the definition? (e.g., (Zhang et al., 2026), UN)

MIS.findings.text: What are the findings regarding misinformation?

MIS.has_def.text: Is there a definition of misinformation?

MIS.is_present.text: Is misinformation present? It is considered DIRECT when the study names misinformation or disinformation in its own framing, and INDIRECT when it is studied via adjacent or proxy constructs without naming it (e.g., propaganda, fake news).

MIS.metrics.text: What metrics are reported? (How do they measure misinformation?)

MIS.metrics_desc.text: Cite any relevant descriptions of the metrics.

labels: inoculation (e.g., pre-emptively provide correct information, warn people they may be misinformed)
technological solutions (e.g., early detection of malicious accounts, ranking and selection algorithms)
MIS.responses.text: Are responses to misinformation presented? If so, which? (Categories based on Treen et al., 2020)

MIS.truth_status.text: How is truth status established? (e.g., professional fact checkers, scientific-expert judgement, source-level credibility heuristic, crowd labels, LLM judgement)

MIS.type.text: What is the type of misinformation? (e.g., conspiracy theories, climate denial)

labels: Classical ML (LR, SVM, NB, RF, gradient boosting)
ML.method.text: Which computational method do they use?

ML.subtechnique.text: Which ML subtechniques or frameworks are used?

ML.task.text: Which ML task(s) do they tackle?

labels: 1 = generic "this could be useful for practitioners" gesture
2 = concrete implications for a named actor and decision
3 = an artifact usable for decision-making (deployed tool, dashboard, released system, intervention design)
4 = evaluated in a real decision context or with the intended users
MOT.action.text: Is the methodology actionable? (“Actionability refers to the degree to which the method proposed enables decision-making or intervention”, definition modified from (Delobelle et al., 2024))

labels: transfer to a new language or platform
MOT.motiv_cat.text: Under which categories do those motivations fall?

MOT.motiv_cite.text: What are the motivation(s) of the study? Cite them.

MOT.motiv_clear.text: Is there a clear motivation in terms of climate, misinformation, or polarization besides just an improvement on machine learning metrics?

MOT.motiv_clear_cite.text: Which passage states it? Cite and/or explain.

labels: 1 = construct defined but measure not linked to the definition
3 = explicit link, measure justified against the stated definition
4 = explicit link plus validation (human validation, sensitivity analysis, comparison of alternative operationalizations)
MOT.theory.text: Is there a theoretical basis for the methodological approach? That is, does the methodology they define align with the construct they measure? E.g., the definition of polarization matches the metrics of polarization they propose.

MOT.validation.text: What type of validation was used?

MP.rel_cite.text: Cite the text stating the concluding relationship between misinformation and polarization

MP.rel_claimed.condition: POL.is_present in ('yes, direct', 'yes, indirect') AND MIS.is_present in ('yes, direct', 'yes, indirect')
labels: common cause, both are attributed to a third factor
MP.rel_claimed.text: What relationship between misinformation and polarization does the paper claim to have shown?

labels: descriptive co-occurrence, both constructs observed in the same corpus, no statistic relating them
correlation, chi-square, or similar bivariate association
temporal precedence, lagged models, time-ordered measurement, change-point alignment
network evidence, e.g. community structure, exposure paths, diffusion within or across clusters
MP.rel_evidence.text: What evidence does the paper offer in support of the relationship it claims to have shown?

MP.rel_measured.condition: POL.is_present in ('yes, direct', 'yes, indirect') AND MIS.is_present in ('yes, direct', 'yes, indirect')
labels: common cause, both are attributed to a third factor
MP.rel_measured.text: What relationship between misinformation and polarisation do the paper's measures and analysis support?

POL.change.text: What is the change in polarization?

POL.def.text: What definition of polarization does the study state? Cite it.

POL.def_src.text: What is the source of the definition? (e.g., (Zhang et al., 2026), UN)

POL.findings.text: What are the findings regarding polarization?

POL.has_def.text: Is there a definition of polarization?

POL.is_present.text: Is polarization present? It is considered DIRECT when the study names polarization in its own framing, and INDIRECT when it is studied via adjacent or proxy constructs without naming it (e.g., network or community analysis, echo chambers, homophily, changes in discourse).

POL.type.text: What is the type of polarization? (e.g., political polarization, affective polarization)

labels: 1 = generic "this could be useful for practitioners" gesture
3 = involved in design or evaluation (participatory, co-design, they evaluated outputs)
